title: fix(cli): a serve boot that composes no HTTP server stays up until it is stopped
body:
Fixes #23744

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`os serve objectstack.config.ts --no-server --preset minimal`, in production on a host config with no `OS_DATABASE_URL` and no auth secret, printed its ready banner ending `Press Ctrl+C to stop` and then exited 0 by itself, about 50 ms later. This happened with and without an `ipc` channel, and before any signal. The process emitted `beforeExit`, so this was the event loop draining. `process.exit()` does not emit `beforeExit`, so the kernel's signal path did not end it. Nothing on that path calls `kernel.shutdown()`, so no plugin `destroy()` ran either.

## Which reading: "stay up", established by measurement

The card left the defect to the claimant: is a kernel-only boot meant to stay up, or to run and exit? The measurements below all point the same way: it is meant to stay up.

**1. The lifetime came from the storage driver, not from a decision.** These readings were taken at base `adce192974`, spawning the built CLI (`bin/run.js`, `NODE_ENV` unset). A `--require` preload recorded the ref'd handles and timers, with their creation stacks, 5 to 12 s after spawn.

| boot (production unless `--dev`) | what held the event loop | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-server --preset minimal`, no driver, with `ipc` | nothing (`beforeExit` at +4275 ms: only the stdout/stderr pipes) | banner +4329 ms, `seed-settled` +4330 ms, **exit 0 at +4387 ms, no signal** |
| the same, without `ipc` | nothing | banner +3997 ms, **exit 0 at +4046 ms** |
| `--no-server --preset minimal` + `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:./a.db` | ONLY `setInterval(1000)` from tarn's `KnexPool._startReaping` | alive 8 s past its banner; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |
| `--no-server` (default preset: job, queue, messaging composed) + DB + auth secret | ONLY the same tarn reaper | alive 8 s; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |
| `--dev --no-server` (`SqlDriver(better-sqlite3) → :memory:`) | ONLY the same tarn reaper | alive 15 s; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |

The same command, with the same preset, stays up or exits depending on whether the driver keeps a connection pool. The job and queue services do not hold the loop. The platform's background loops are `unref()`ed on purpose ("the loop never keeps a process alive by itself", `DispatchLoop` in `packages/core/src/dispatch-loop.ts`), so the host is meant to decide the lifetime. On a kernel-only boot, the host is `os serve`, and before this change it did not decide.

**2. Everything else already says "stay up":**
- the banner's `Press Ctrl+C to stop`;
- `serve.ts`'s own comment at the end of the ready path: "No duplicate handler needed here — just keep the process alive";
- the kernel's `gracefulShutdown` contract: the kernel owns the process, and a signal drains it and then exits;
- the docs: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` says "Skip HTTP server (kernel only)" and "Toggle HTTP server plugin", and `packages/cli/README.md` says "Skip starting HTTP server plugin". None of them says the boot runs once.

**3. A run-and-exit kernel boot already exists, and it is explicit.** `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` shuts the kernel down and calls `process.exit(0)` before any banner.

**4. Who runs a kernel-only boot (tree `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `adce192974`, `git grep -- --no-server`):**
- Every boot that is meant to exit sets `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1`:
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.boot-parity.integration.test.ts:99`
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.telemetry-sibling.integration.test.ts:119`
  - `packages/cli/test/serve-migrate-exit-schema-parity.integration.test.ts`
  - `serve.ts` also names cloud's `apps/cloud/scripts/migrate.ts`. It is not in this repository and was not measured.
- Every other `--no-server` boot is stopped by a signal:
  - `serve-no-server-banner.integration.test.ts`
  - `serve-no-transport-announcements.integration.test.ts`, whose header already calls the self-exit "a separate card"
  - `test/serve-no-storage-boot-guard.integration.test.ts`
- `os dev` and `os start` never pass `--no-server`. No script, workflow, example or Dockerfile runs it.
- Count of readers that run a plain `--no-server` boot and expect it to exit: **0**.

The evidence is not split, so the banner line stays and the process now matches it.

## The fix

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`:
- `holdKernelOnlyProcess(kernel)`: one ref'd `setInterval` whose callback does nothing. Its period is the largest a Node timer accepts. It is a handle, not a timeout: it ends nothing and decides nothing.
- The kernel's own shutdown releases it, through `kernel.onShutdown`. So the kernel's SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGQUIT handling stays the only thing that ends the process, and the process exits with the kernel's code.
- ⛔ No signal listener is added.
- It is called at the end of the ready path only when `httpServer !== 'composed'`. That is the same composition read the banner's address rows and the `publishBoundPort` gate already use, so all three agree on whether there is a transport.

Unchanged:
- a composed boot, including `--no-server` with a config-mounted `HonoServerPlugin`;
- `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1`;
- `publishBoundPort` and its channels, and the `MCP:` gate;
- the banner text, `utils/format.ts` and the docs, because the behaviour they state is now true.

## After, at the same door (built CLI at `c29a1d1f90`)

| boot | outcome |
|---|---|
| prod `--no-server --preset minimal`, `ipc` | banner +4254 ms; alive 5 s later; at +7002 ms the only ref'd timer is `holdKernelOnlyProcess`'s; SIGTERM, then **exit 0, signal null** |
| the same, without `ipc` | alive 5 s; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |
| default composed production boot | `[objectstack:listening, objectstack:seed-settled]`; alive 5 s; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |
| `--dev --no-server` | alive 5 s; SIGTERM, then exit 0 |
| `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1 --no-server --preset minimal` + DB | exit 0 at +4.6 s, no banner (unchanged) |

## Pins

- `src/commands/serve-kernel-only-lifetime.integration.test.ts` is the fixed shape at the door. It spawns `bin/run.js` with an `ipc` channel and a hard timeout on the boot (150 s) and on the stop (60 s). Each child is SIGKILLed in `finally` if it is still alive. It runs three boots, and for each one waits for the banner and `seed-settled`, leaves it alone for 3 s, then sends SIGTERM:
  - the card's command: still alive, and SIGTERM ends it with `{ code: 0, signal: null }`;
  - CONTROL `--dev --no-server`: the same;
  - CONTROL default composed boot: `[listening, seed-settled]`, alive, `{ code: 0, signal: null }`.
- `src/commands/serve-kernel-only-hold.test.ts` (unit) runs against a real `ObjectKernel`:
  - the handle is ref'd;
  - it is released by the kernel's `shutdown()` and by nothing before it.

  It also carries comment-masked source pins:
  - exactly one hold site, gated on `httpServer !== 'composed'`, after `seedSettlement.release()`;
  - `serve.ts` installs no `process.on('SIG…')` listener.

## Negative control (ablation)

The fix was committed first, at `7438857540`. The script was trap-restored, and every path in it was absolute.
- `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced `if (httpServer !== 'composed') holdKernelOnlyProcess(kernel);` with `void 'ABLATION_23744_NO_HOLD';`: anchor x1 → x0, marker x0 → x1, blob `ee844f32bdfc` → `98880fdd130a`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build` exited 0. `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/cli ABLATION_23744_NO_HOLD` found the marker in `dist/commands/serve.js` (exit 0), and the dist call-site count was 0.
- **Integration: RED, bounded.** The card's command failed after 4491 ms with `expected { code: 0, signal: null, msAfterBanner: 50 } to be null`. Both controls stayed green.
- **Unit: RED** on both wiring pins: 2 failed, 4 passed.
- Restore: the blob equals HEAD `ee844f32bdfc` and `git diff HEAD` is empty. The rebuild exited 0. `--absent` preflight exited 0 (marker absent from all 652 built files, tree clean), and the dist call-site count was back to 1. Integration was green 3/3 and unit green 6/6.

## Tests and gates (final head `bd15f3ad43`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project integration` over the new file and the three sibling `--no-server` integration files: **4 files, 15 tests passed**. Run locally because this diff adds an integration file.
- The new unit file: 6/6.
- The full `unit` tier of `@objectstack/cli`: **307 files, 4573 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` plus `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `pnpm exec eslint` over the three changed `.ts` files: exit 0.
- Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` gave 66 commands. All 66 were run at `bd15f3ad43` and every one exited 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads `66 derived, 66 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (exit 0). In an earlier pass two families answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3), because nine packages outside this diff were unbuilt. Those packages were built and both families re-ran green. The derivation warns that the tree is 7 commits behind `origin/main` and that `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` has changed there since; CI reads the new copy.
- CI runs the rest of the farm.

## Acceptance notes

- **A comment this change made stale (outside the claim's file surface, so not edited here).** `serve-no-transport-announcements.integration.test.ts`'s header says "Shape 1 exits on its own a few milliseconds after its banner (a separate card)". It no longer does. That file's directory watch still has a reason to exist: it catches a state file written and then deleted mid-boot. Suggested one-line correction for whoever next touches that file: "Shape 1 stays up until it is stopped (#23744)".
- **Branch not merged with `origin/main` before opening.** Seven commits landed on `main` after `adce192974`. None touches `packages/cli`, `packages/runtime` or the kernel lifecycle; they touch `spec`, `core` (api-key text), `rest`, `plugin-security` and docs. Nothing conflicts textually. The queue rebuilds on merged `main`.
- **Budget.** The integration file declares `// test-budget: 40` in the class "spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture". It does three boots, each differing only in the input under test, held 3 s each. Local readings were 26.2 s and 27.0 s on a shared container; 27.0 × 1.25, rounded up, gives 40. There is no CI reading yet.
- **Not covered here.** A pool configured with `min: 0` would let tarn stop reaping after its idle timeout, so the old self-exit could also have reached a driver-backed boot after about 30 s idle. This was not measured: the hold makes the lifetime independent of the driver either way.
